title: Weighted Service Classes and Predictive Autoscale for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a mechanism to offer weighted service classes across dedicated GPU pools and a predictive autoscaler that respects per-customer throughput guarantees. This ticket scopes design and an initial rollout for: (1) assigning weighted service classes to customer lanes (gold/silver/bronze or numeric weights), (2) enforcing weighted fair share during overload and isolation events, and (3) a predictive autoscaling controller that anticipates demand spikes and scales pool capacity before SLOs degrade.

Background & Motivation:
Customers on Dedicated capacity require predictable throughput and graceful degradation when the fleet is constrained. Current hard-quotas and binary reservations lead to inefficient GPU utilization and customer-visible tail latency during tenant spikes. We need a flexible policy that: (a) provides differentiated guarantees without underutilizing hardware, (b) mitigates noisy cross-customer interference, and (c) integrates with our autoscale/placement pipeline to proactively add capacity for forecasted load.

Goals:
- Define a small set of weighted service class primitives (weight, min-guarantee, burst-capacity) that map to runtime scheduling behavior.
- Implement enforcement in the GPU lane allocator so steady-state fairness follows weights and min-guarantees.
- Add an autoscale controller using short-term demand prediction (sliding-window time-series model) to trigger preemptive scale actions for Dedicated pools.
- Ensure fallbacks: when autoscale cannot add capacity, the allocator performs proportional degradation by weight with clear telemetry and customer-visible signals.

Non-goals:
- Full multi-region reshuffling.
- Replacing existing hard-slice reservations for customers who explicitly purchased guaranteed instances; those remain first-class.

Design notes:
- Service class schema: {name, weight (int), min_rps (optional), burst_multiplier (float)} (implemented as flat config keyed by customer-lane).
- Runtime enforcement approach: token-bucket per lane plus scheduler weight factoring in queue depth and KV cache hits. During overload, scheduler demotes non-min-guarantee requests first and enforces weighted token drain.
- Predictive autoscale: lightweight ARIMA-inspired exponential smoothing on per-lane RPS + model confidence threshold; if predicted 95th-percentile exceeds capacity margin for X minutes, create scale request to fleet autoscaler.
- Safety: autoscale proposals carry TTL and must be approved by placement limits; rollback if scale fails in 10m and degradation SLO breaches.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for allocator weight enforcement and token-bucket behavior.
- Predictive autoscaler triggers scale proposals in synthetic spike tests and does not flip-flop for noisy signals (hysteresis).
- Observability surfaced: per-lane p50/p95/p99 latency, lane throughput, weight-violation events, autoscale decisions with reasoning trace.
- No regressions on Dedicated customers with hard reservations; validation via e2e CI scenario.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Config + schema (2d): add service-class config and validation to control-plane API.
2) Runtime allocator changes (6d): token-bucket, queue-prioritization, weighted drain logic; unit tests.
3) Predictive autoscaler (4d): aggregation pipeline, prediction model, decision logic, safe-guard TTL.
4) Rollout & Observability (4d): expose metrics/dashboards and add feature flag gating.
5) Canary (2 weeks): enable for internal customers and 2 low-risk external customers, monitor SLOs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Incorrect weight tuning can starve smaller lanes: mitigate by requiring min_rps for any lane receiving weight > 1 and adding soft-fairness clamps.
- Autoscale false positives leading to cost blowouts: mitigate via confidence thresholds, rate-limits on scale-ups, and manual approval for large increases.
- Scheduler complexity increasing latency: microbench runtime in canary and keep code path opt-in behind feature flag.

Rollout plan and rollback criteria:
- Feature gated. Start with internal staging pools; if p95 latency increases by >20% for any lane, immediately disable weighted enforcement and fall back to current behavior. If autoscaler induces repeated failed scale actions (>3 in 1h), pause predictive autoscale and keep manual scaling.

comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha: Initial ticket created; added high-level design and goals. Linked RFC and dashboard mock.
2026-02-15 - Design review (Luca, Maria, Chen): Agreed on token-bucket enforcement and predictive autoscale approach. Maria requested clearer min_rps semantics; action added to schema doc.
2026-02-20 - ENG-31209 referenced as dependency for allocator refactor (existing workstream).

2026-02-25 - Load test 1: synthetic 5x spike on silver lanes. Outcome: weighted drain prevented complete starvation but revealed a KV-cache thrash causing 18% p99 regression. Filed follow-up ENG-544000 to improve cache affinity (placeholder).
2026-02-28 - PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/1280 (adds weight enforcement + token-bucket). Seeking review from runtime team.
2026-03-04 - Code review feedback from Chen: simplify weight normalization to avoid integer overflow; Luca updated implementation, new benchmarks added.
2026-03-08 - Canary prep: feature flag ready, integration tests green. Added dashboards to staging Grafana and alert thresholds for weight-violation events.

2026-03-10 - Autoscaler prototype ran in staging for 48h. Triggered 4 scale proposals; 3 executed successfully. Noted one delayed placement due to capacity constraints in region us-west-2. Will add region-aware backoff.
2026-03-10 - Decision: security review required for autoscale decision authority; ticket assigned to SecOps for review in week 2026-W11.
notes: Follow-on work may include finer-grained cache affinity and region-aware predictive placement. Coordinate with capacity planning and sales for customers with contractual throughput SLAs.
